## When to recognise the pattern

When subproblems overlap and you need an optimal value or count.

## The key question

**How do you transform a story into a recurrence without writing code first?**

## Formula worth memorising

$$
F(i)=F(i-1)+F(i-2),\quad F(0)=1,\ F(1)=1
$$

**Every symbol explained:** F(i) is the number of distinct ways to climb i steps using 1-step or 2-step moves; i is a nonnegative integer. F(0)=1 counts the empty sequence of moves, and F(1)=1 counts one single step.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For i=2, F(2)=F(1)+F(0)=1+1=2: [1,1] or [2]. For i=3, F(3)=F(2)+F(1)=2+1=3: [1,1,1], [1,2], [2,1].

## Why this is mathematically correct

Every valid sequence ends with either one step from i−1 or two from i−2. These final-move classes are mutually exclusive and exhaustive, so their counts add. Caching subproblem values prevents exponential recomputation.

## Limits and counterexamples

The recurrence changes if allowed move lengths change. In optimisation DP, replace addition of counts with min/max of costs; always distinguish counting from choosing the best.

## The 20-second memory card

**Memorise: Define the meaning of state F(i), partition solutions by last decision, prove the recurrence, state base cases.**

Now reproduce the equation, example and proof aloud, without looking.

**Interview problems:** Climbing Stairs; House Robber.
